label: FLAWS_general_c3_v2
original_text: ensuring they were first posted on arXiv after the knowledge cutoff dates of the models we plan to test.
modified_text: ensuring their most recent revision on arXiv was posted after the knowledge cutoff dates of the models we plan to test.
explanation: The mechanism of this error is **temporal data leakage via versioning**. The flaw is substituting the date of the "most recent revision" for the "first posted" date. A paper could have its first version (v1) posted before the knowledge cutoff, with its core ideas and text becoming part of the training data. A later revision (v2, v3) with minor changes or additions posted after the cutoff would be incorrectly selected as "new" data, leading to contamination. A researcher might plausibly make this mistake while trying to use the most "up-to-date" version of a paper for evaluation.
reasoning: The error introduces a data leakage vector by using a "most recent revision" date instead of the "first posted" date, which would allow information from older versions of papers to contaminate the "new" data, thus undermining the premise of evaluating models on unseen information.
